target_customer: People and businesses searching for and buying domain names (affiliate commissions); at the 2022 batch, software companies buying creator marketing through Strobe
problem: Finding an available domain name quickly; the YC launch product Strobe aimed to help software companies find influencers who already like their product.
business_model: Affiliate commissions on domain purchases through partner links, now also an ICANN accredited registrar; Strobe was a subscription web app
product_category: Domain search tools (consumer and developer tools), plus an AI creator marketing tool at the batch

founders.name: Beau Hartshorne
prior_employers: Facebook (early employee, growth, photos and mobile teams)
previous_startups: Snipshot (online image editor, 2006; outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. Instant described itself as from the first Y Combinator batch in its own post.

founders.name: Dirkjan Ochtman
founders.background_notes: YC page: professional Rust open source maintainer (rustls, instant-distance).

technical_complexity.rationale: Fast domain availability search is engineering heavy on latency but well understood, and the company had run it since 2005; Strobe used LLMs on social data.

defensibility.rationale: Long standing product with search traffic and an exact name domain, but registrars and other search tools offer similar functions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not found. The company stayed independent and in 2026 moved to become a registrar and rebranded to instant.ai.

market_need_then: The site reported over 2.5M searches and 250K domains purchased from its free tool by the time of the YC page, showing steady consumer demand for domain search.

branding.name_origin: Company describes starting in 2005 as a fast domain search engine, hence Instant; no further explanation sourced.
branding.domain_note: Product at instantdomainsearch.com; company later acquired instant.ai (a podcast episode mentions the purchase; date and price not found) and instant.ca redirects to it.

identity.logo: Lightning bolt, kept through the 2026 rebrand
identity.voice_and_tone: Describes itself as a research lab building tools to go from idea to something real

branding.brand_signature: The lightning bolt and the speed of as-you-type search

rebrands.why: Expansion beyond domain search into registrar, API and other tools, per the company changelog

branding.community_and_virality: Long running product with nearly half a billion searches across 80 plus countries per the company; covered by Domain Name Wire in 2026.

brand_strength.rationale: Two decades of use and a descriptive but recognizable name; generic naming limits distinctiveness.

pivots.to: Strobe, AI creator marketing tool, launched around the YC batch
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; inferred from the YC launch page

outcome_analysis: Instant Labs is active. Its domain search business, started in 2005, kept growing (the company reports 2.5x growth in the last year as of its instant.ai post) and in 2026 it moved into registrar services and an API under the instant.ai brand. The YC era Strobe creator marketing product appears peripheral. Investors are named by the company but amounts are not disclosed.
notes: Company pages say it has been backed by Slow Ventures and Y Combinator since 2022, and the GitHub profile adds Form Capital and Tiny Capital; no round dates or amounts found, and an aggregator lists a different investor set, so no round is recorded. Competitor searches returned no sources dated near the batch, so the list is empty; Domainr appeared only as a Dealroom entry. The Strobe pivot date is approximate and unsourced beyond the batch. CEO listing conflicts between company pages (Matt Maiale versus Hartshorne).
